title: Amazon shares fall as weaker Q4 outlook offsets 39% AWS growth
detail:
Amazon shares fall as weaker Q4 outlook offsets 39% AWS growth

Amazon shares fall as weaker Q4 outlook offsets 39% AWS growth Proactive uses images sourced from Shutterstock

Amazon.com Inc (NASDAQ:AMZN) shares fell around 6% on Thursday evening after the e-commerce and cloud computing giant issued fourth-quarter guidance that fell short of expectations, overshadowing strong growth at Amazon Web Services (AWS).

The company reported third-quarter revenue of $201.9 billion, up 12% year over year but slightly below analyst expectations of $202.3 billion. Earnings per share of $1.89 also missed the $1.96 consensus estimate, despite operating income of $28.1 billion beating forecasts of $26.2 billion.

AWS was a bright spot, with sales rising 39% to $46 billion, its fastest growth rate in nearly five years and ahead of estimates of $45.4 billion. AWS operating income reached $17.8 billion, while the cloud division's annualized revenue run rate exceeded $184 billion.

However, Amazon's fourth-quarter revenue forecast of $240 billion to $247 billion came in below the $244.5 billion consensus estimate at the midpoint. The company forecast operating income of $28.5 billion to $33.5 billion, with the midpoint also below expectations of $33.1 billion.

Advertising revenue was another area of weakness, rising to $19.6 billion but missing estimates of $20.87 billion. North American sales of $112.9 billion and international revenue of $43.1 billion also came in slightly below expectations.

Investors also weighed Amazon's growing investment requirements as it expands its artificial intelligence infrastructure.

Capital expenditure reached $77.3 billion in the third quarter, well above analyst estimates of $57.5 billion. Free cash flow over the trailing 12 months was negative $42.4 billion, highlighting the near-term financial pressure from its investment programme.

CEO Andy Jassy pointed to significant growth opportunities in cloud computing and AI, saying he expects AWS to grow by more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028.

"There has never been a trillion dollar revenue business, and we may have two of them in the next 5-10 years," Jassy said.

Amazon also reported continued adoption of its AI-related services. Its AgentCore platform serves tens of thousands of customers, with the number of agents deployed doubling in the third quarter. Alexa for Shopping has more than 400 million customers, with interactions increasing 570% year over year.

Net income also included a $9.5 billion pre-tax gain related to Anthropic, recorded in non-operating income. The investment gain contributed to reported earnings, underscoring the importance of separating underlying operating performance from gains tied to Amazon's AI investments.

While AWS growth and demand for AI infrastructure remain central to Amazon's longer-term outlook, the latest results left investors weighing those opportunities against a softer near-term forecast, rising capital expenditure and pressure on free cash flow.

title: Amazon's 3Q results miss analysts' estimates, but posts solid sales gains in cloud computing unit
detail:
Amazon's 3Q results miss analysts' estimates, but posts solid sales gains in cloud computing unit

Trade AMZN on Coinbase

NEW YORK (AP) — Amazon offered a cautious sales outlook for the current fourth quarter that encompasses the critical holiday shopping period after delivering fiscal third-quarter results that came in below Wall Street analysts' expectations.

The Seattle-based company, however, posted strong growth in its prominent cloud computing unit. Sales in its cloud computing unit called AWS rose 39.3% during the latest quarter ended Sept. 30, higher than the 37% clip in the previous quarter. It marked the fastest growth rate in nearly five years, the company said.

Still, shares were down more than 6% in after-market trading when the results were released as investors focused on the core business.

Analysts will be looking for any comments from Amazon executives on the earnings call Thursday about the holiday shopping season. The tech giant said earlier this month that it would hire 300,000 U.S. seasonal workers for the shopping period. That's up from 250,000 last year.

Investors also have been closely watching Amazon's quarterly earnings to see if the company's big spending on artificial intelligence is starting to pay off.

CEO and President Andy Jassy disclosed to investors in July that it now expects capital spending, mostly in artificial intelligence, to total $220 billion. That number includes outlays on robots, semiconductors and satellites. That's up from the $200 billion investment plan that was announced in February and well above the $128 billion in capital spending for all of last year. Jassy had cited the higher cost of memory chips as the main reason for the increase.

Jassy told investors this past summer that even at the $220 billion level, Amazon will not have enough capacity to meet all of the demand it has this year.

The latest earnings report from Alphabet late Wednesday raised alarm bells when it reported weaker growth for the summer than analysts expected. The company behind Google and YouTube also said it burned through more cash during the latest quarter, according to a measure called free cash flow, after its purchases of property and equipment topped $51 billion. Its stock plummeted Thursday.

Such worries are weighing on the entire AI industry following a big push to build data centers and fill them with AI chips.

Amazon reported net income of $20.69 billion, or $1.89 per share, in the three-month period. That compares with $21.19 billion, or $1.95 per share, in the year-ago period.

Sales rose to $201.94 billion, compared with the same year-ago period's $180.17 billion.

SEATTLE (AP) — SEATTLE (AP) — Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) on Thursday reported third-quarter net income of $20.69 billion.

On a per-share basis, the Seattle-based company said it had net income of $1.89.

The results fell short of Wall Street expectations. The average estimate of 14 analysts surveyed by Zacks Investment Research was for earnings of $2.01 per share.

The online retailer posted revenue of $201.94 billion in the period, also falling short of Street forecasts. Eleven analysts surveyed by Zacks expected $202.11 billion.

For the current quarter ending in December, Amazon said it expects revenue in the range of $240 billion to $247 billion.

Amazon shares have risen slightly more than 6% since the beginning of the year, while the S&P's 500 index has climbed 13%. In the final minutes of trading on Thursday, shares hit $245.42, a climb of nearly 7% in the last 12 months.

title: Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) posts Q3 2026 sales in line with estimates but stock drops
detail:
Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) posts Q3 2026 sales in line with estimates but stock drops
Anthony Lee
Thu, October 29, 2026 at 4:15 PM EDT 4 min read
AMZN
Trade AMZN on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Cloud computing and online retailer Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) met Wall Street's revenue expectations in Q3 2026, with revenue rising 12.1% year on year to $201.9 billion. The company expects next quarter's revenue to be around $243.5 billion, close to analysts' consensus estimates. Its GAAP profit of $1.89 per share was 3.5% below analysts' consensus estimates.

For more on Amazon, read our full research report.

Amazon (AMZN) Q3 2026 highlights:

Revenue $201.9 billion vs S&P analysts' consensus estimates of $202.3 billion (in line)

AWS revenue beat but Advertising revenue missed

EPS (GAAP) $1.89 vs analysts' consensus estimates of $1.96 (3.5% miss)

Operating margin 13.9%, up from 9.7% in the same quarter last year

Free cash flow margin -17.3%, down from 0.7% in the same quarter last year

Market capitalization $2.75 trillion

"Our AWS investment in functionality and infrastructure is working, with over 39% year-over-year revenue growth in Q3 ($184 billion revenue run rate) and projected revenue growth rates of over 40% both in 2027 and in 2028," said Andy Jassy, President and CEO, Amazon. "Our broader selection and speedier delivery are helping us capture more retail market segment share with improving margins, and our newer businesses, ranging from Grocery to Pharmacy to Amazon Leo to Zoox are progressing encouragingly. There has never been a trillion dollar revenue business, and we may have two of them in the next 5-10 years."

Revenue growth

Amazon shows that even companies of its scale can grow quickly. The company's revenue base of $458 billion five years ago has increased to $797.5 billion in the last year, translating into an impressive 11.7% annualized growth rate.

Over the same period, Amazon's big tech peers Alphabet, Microsoft and Apple posted annualized growth rates of 14.5%, 14.5% and 5.2%, respectively. This is an important consideration because investors often use the comparisons as a starting point for their valuations. Relative to these benchmarks, Amazon's price appears fair.

Long-term growth matters, but for big tech companies, a half-decade historical view may miss emerging trends in AI. Amazon's annualized revenue growth of 13.4% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, suggesting its demand was strong and recently accelerated.

This quarter, Amazon's year-on-year revenue growth was 12.1%, and its $201.9 billion of revenue was in line with Wall Street's consensus estimates. Company management is currently guiding for a 14.1% year-on-year increase in revenue next quarter. This projection is strong for a company of its scale and indicates that the market sees some success for its newer products.
